name: Itemized
oneLiner: This month's thermal receipt for $10,000 of donated Google Ads, stamped COMPLIANT, on a cool gray counter.
concept:
The buyer wants proof they can forward, not a promise they have to believe. Itemized makes proof of spend literal: the hero object is this month's receipt for the Google Ad Grant, printed on white thermal paper with perforated edges, in monospace, with dotted leaders. Search ads served, clicks, a click-through rate above Google's 5% floor, conversions, policy checks passed 14 of 14, ad spend against the $10,000 cap, then a double rule, PAID BY GOOGLE, and a total that reads DUE FROM YOU $0.00. Under it: PAID BY GOOGLE · MANAGED BY NONPROFIT MEGAPHONE, a named account lead who replies in a business day, a barcode, and one rubber stamp in green ink that says COMPLIANT. The joke is dry and structural: the most official-looking document on the page is the one that costs the nonprofit nothing, and every claim the company makes becomes a line item with a figure beside it.

Around the paper the site is calm and technical. The ground is a cool light gray (#EFF1F3, not warm, not white) so the receipt reads as paper lying on a counter; the ink is near-black; headlines are Geist at large size; the receipt and every label on the page are JetBrains Mono; and there is no colour at all except the stamp's green, which the buttons and the eligibility link borrow. No cards, no charts with axes, no gradients, no radii, one paper shadow. The register is radical transparency with a straight face: what you got, what it cost, who paid, who checked. It suits Nonprofit Megaphone because the company's real advantage is documentary (780+ accounts, $48M+ of donated media, a guarantee in writing, monthly reporting, an endorsement from Google's first Head of Ad Grants) and a receipt is the most trusted document ordinary people handle.
distinctFrom: It is the only direction built around a single physical paper object (a monospace thermal receipt with perforated edges) on a cool gray counter with green as the sole colour, where the others are editorial grids, dashboards, civic blocks or warm paper.
bullets: The hero is this month's receipt for $10,000 of Google Ads.
Cool gray counter, white thermal paper, one ink, one green stamp.
Every claim becomes a mono line item with a figure beside it.
rightFor: A leadership team willing to publish real monthly figures and be held to them, selling to buyers who prize transparency over warmth.
needs: One client's consent for a real receipt
A monthly receipt in the reporting pipeline
Wordmark reset to Geist, mark redrawn

palette.note: Cool light gray, the page ground everywhere. Deliberately not warm and not white, so the receipt reads as paper lying on a counter rather than a card on a page, and so the direction cannot be mistaken for Public Works (white) or Amplitude (warm paper).

Pure white, used only for paper objects: the hero receipt, the three statements in section 02, the fee receipt in 04 and the CTA band. Every paper has perforated top and bottom edges (CSS clip-path) and the site's single drop shadow (0 16px 24px at 16% ink). Nothing else on the site is white.
Near-black ink for headlines, body, the receipt's print, the ink rules above major sections and the megaphone mark. 15.7:1 on the counter, 17.8:1 on paper.

Cool gray for labels, the receipt's notes, fine print and the roll caption. 6.05:1 on the counter and 6.85:1 on paper, so 11px labels pass AA with margin. The receipt's dashed rules are #9AA0A8 (decorative, 2.6:1).
Hairline gray for the nav rule, column rules, the dotted leaders on every line item and the trust-strip divider. The site's structural device, together with the ink rule above major sections.
Zebra rows in the terms table, disabled states and the eligibility checker's track. Never a fill behind body text.

The only chromatic colour on the site. The COMPLIANT stamp, both buttons, the eligibility underline, PAID BY GOOGLE in the eyebrow, the active nav underline, 'Cleared' on the receipt, the 3px focus ring and Michelle Hurtado's title. 4.69:1 on the counter and 5.31:1 on paper; white on it 5.31:1. Used for emphasis only at 11px and above with weight 600 or 700.
Hover and active state for the green button and the eligibility link; white on it 7.74:1. Never a fill on its own.

typography.scaleNotes: h1 62px / 1.0 / -0.035em, Geist 600, tabular numerals so '$10,000' sets like a figure, three lines in the 608px copy column; 40px / 1.02 on phones. No italic and no colour in headlines: the headline's emphasis device is the object beside it. h2 46px / 1.05 / -0.03em Geist 600 with a mono section number ('01') before it. h3 24px / 1.2. Deck 17px / 1.5 Geist 400 in ink, max 560px, with one 600-weight clause; body 17px / 1.5, max 66ch; phone body 16px / 1.48. Fine print 14px in secondary gray, never the only place a required fact appears. Pull quote (Hurtado) 17px / 1.4 Geist with a mono attribution. Everything else is mono: labels 11.5px JetBrains Mono 500 uppercase +0.06em (11px on phones, the floor); eyebrow 12px uppercase +0.06em with 7px ink squares as separators; the nav's CLIENT REPORTS link 12px; button tags 11px uppercase after a hairline. The receipt: 12px / 1.45 JetBrains Mono, uppercase line items at +0.02em, figures at weight 500 with tabular-nums, notes 11px / 1.25 in faded ink, the header 14px 700 at +0.16em, the SAMPLE tag 11px 700 at +0.12em in a 1.5px ink box, DUE FROM YOU 13px 700 with the $0.00 at 26px 700 / -0.02em (24px on phones), the tail 11px / 1.6 uppercase, and PLEASE RETAIN FOR YOUR BOARD 11.5px 700 at +0.12em. The stamp's SVG text is sized in viewBox units so it renders at 11.2px (desktop) and 11.1px (phone) for the small lines and 21px for COMPLIANT. 'On file' line items 12.5px mono with 11.5px uppercase labels; client roll 12px mono uppercase +0.08em. Buttons 15px / 600 Geist, 16.5px vertical padding (48px tall), 0 radius; compact nav button 14px / 600 at 40px. Rules: 1px #D3D7DC hairlines, a 1px ink rule above the trust strip and above the copy column's foot, 1.5px dashed #9AA0A8 and 3px double ink rules inside the receipt only. Radii: none anywhere (the stamp's 3px corner is drawn in the SVG, not a card).

layout:
- Grid and rhythm: 12 columns, 1200px container, 48px side margins (16px on phone), 8px base spacing. Vertical rhythm is set by rules and by paper objects, not by card padding: a 1px hairline under the nav, a 1px ink rule above the trust strip and above each numbered section. The only white on the site is paper, and every paper has perforated top and bottom edges and one drop shadow. No radii, no gradients, no charts with axes: numbers are always line items with dotted leaders. Accessibility contract shared with the other directions: 48px targets, 3px green focus ring, 17px body, AA at every size, CSS-only reveals.
- 0. Nav (68px, hairline beneath). Megaphone mark redrawn in ink only, 'Nonprofit Megaphone' in Geist 600 18px. Links: Ad Grant, Services, Case studies, Guides, Team, Pricing; the active link has a 2px green underline. Right: CLIENT REPORTS → as a mono label (the login that signals a real product behind the sales page) and the green 'Book a free call' button, identical to the hero's so the action colour is learned once. No ear strip and no dateline: the receipt carries the date.
- 1. Hero (copy column 608px / paper column 448px, 48px gap, 32px above, the two columns' feet aligned). Copy column: mono eyebrow 'Free search ads for nonprofits · $10,000 a month · PAID BY GOOGLE' (the last item green); h1 '$10,000 of Google Ads a month. Here's the receipt.'; 17px deck ending 'Google pays for the ads. You pay a flat fee.'; action row = green 'Book a free call · 15 MIN' beside the ghost 'See a real receipt · PDF · REDACTED'; the exits line 'Am I eligible?' (green, underlined) with '4 QUESTIONS · NO EMAIL', then 'FLAT MONTHLY FEE · NO % OF AD SPEND' after a hairline; the guarantee line 'Unhappy with the work? Meet our CEO, Amber Snow, and we pay you $25. Our guarantee is a person, not a policy.' The foot of the column, under a 1px ink rule and split by a hairline: left, the Michelle Hurtado endorsement with 'Google's first Head of Ad Grants' in green; right, 'ON FILE · SEP 2026' as four mono line items with dotted leaders (NONPROFITS MANAGED 780+, DONATED MEDIA MANAGED $48M+, GRANT ACQUISITION 100%, CERTIFIED, INAUGURAL 1 of 9). Paper column: the receipt, 400px wide on the counter, perforated top and bottom, one shadow. Centred header NONPROFIT MEGAPHONE / DONATED GOOGLE ADS · MONTHLY RECEIPT / a boxed SAMPLE · AUG 2026 · ILLUSTRATIVE tag; dashed rule; PERIOD 01–31 AUG 2026, PRINTED 01 SEP 2026 · 09:00; dashed rule; SEARCH ADS SERVED 388,412, CLICKS 30,102, CLICK-THROUGH RATE 7.75% with the note 'GOOGLE'S FLOOR 5.00% · Cleared' (Cleared in green), CONVERSIONS 1,214, POLICY CHECKS PASSED 14/14; dashed rule; AD SPEND $9,986.40, GRANT CAP $10,000.00, UNSPENT $13.60 with the note 'does not roll over. we'll get it. 0.1%'; double rule; PAID BY GOOGLE −$9,986.40; DUE FROM YOU $0.00 at 26px; double rule; the tail: PAID BY GOOGLE / MANAGED BY NONPROFIT MEGAPHONE / NAMED ACCOUNT LEAD / REPLIES IN 1 BUSINESS DAY left-aligned beside the COMPLIANT stamp (green, rotated 8°, 'POLICY CHECKS' above and '14/14 · SEP 2026' below the word); dashed rule; barcode; PLEASE RETAIN FOR YOUR BOARD. On load the paper feeds out of the printer in steps and the stamp lands last.
- 2. Trust strip (70px, ink rule above). Left cell 'On file for 780+ nonprofits / ONE RECEIPT EACH · EVERY MONTH'. Right: a static mono roll of eight marks (UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, Solar Sister, AAU, JFCS), set as plain text at 12px uppercase +0.08em, space-between. No carousel, no logos, no slots.
- 3. '01 Google's terms' (full width, then 7/5). The programme's rules typeset as the receipt's terms and conditions: a three-column mono table, Rule / What Google does if you miss it / What we do about it, one row each for the $10,000 monthly cap, the 5% click-through floor and two-month deactivation, mandatory conversion tracking, the keyword quality rules and the annual survey. Beneath it on the right, the eligibility checker: four questions with a green progress rule, honest end states for hospitals, schools and government entities, no email required; the end card offers the call.
- 4. '02 What a month looks like' (three papers, 4/4/4). Three real receipts, redacted (a black mono REDACTED bar, never a blur), from three verticals, each with its own stamp and named account lead. The third shows a month where click-through dipped to 5.4% and lists what the lead changed, because a receipt that only ever says COMPLIANT is a brochure. Each has a 'Forward to board' PDF action.
- 5. '03 Case studies' (4/4/4). Three long-form studies with a fixed KPI trio in mono (click-through, conversion rate, outcome per month) so all 54 read comparably, before/after in tabular figures, a named and titled quote, and a link to the full filterable table with the 12 vertical filters.
- 6. '04 What it costs' (two receipts side by side, 6/6). Google's receipt (DUE FROM YOU $0.00) beside ours: MANAGEMENT FEE (FLAT) with the published figure or range, % OF AD SPEND 0.00%, ONBOARDING with the typical time, MEET-THE-CEO GUARANTEE $25 TO YOU, a 100% acquisition guarantee line, printed in exactly the same grammar. The only receipt on the site where the nonprofit's line is not zero, and it is printed the same way. This is the nav's 'Pricing' anchor.
- 7. '05 Other services' (full width). A hairline-ruled seven-row mono index (Ad Grant, Content, SEO, VisitorEmail, Remarketing, Microsoft Ads, Spanish Ad Creation), each with a one-line description and a 'from' price where leadership will publish one. No icons.
- 8. '06 The people on your account' (full width). Natural-colour team photography with a neutral, slightly cool grade, eye level, rectangular crops on a hairline, 6-up, with 'Nonprofits I support' captions naming real clients; account leads captioned 'signs your receipt'; the cabin-retreat candid as a full-width plate with a credit line; a credentials line (Google Ad Grants Certified Professional, inaugural cohort of nine · Google Partner · Inc. 5000).
- 9. '07 Guides' (5/7). The ungated Ad Grants guide as a featured long read with reading time and last-reviewed date; the latest three posts with dates and bylines.
- 10. CTA band: a full-width strip of white paper with perforated edges, the receipt's tail at page scale. One Geist headline ('Thank you for doing good. Let's spend all of it.'), one green 'Book a free call' button, one mono line of small print with the phone number, 'Am I eligible?' and Amber's email.
- 11. Footer on the counter: four ruled mono columns, the real Beaverton, OR address, Google Partner and Ramp badges, the EmailOctopus field, 'Client reports' login, and a print stylesheet so receipts, case studies and the guarantee page survive being forwarded as PDFs with the perforated edges rendered.
imagery: No illustration system and no stock. The primary visual language is paper objects built in CSS: receipts, statements and the fee receipt, all white, all with perforated top and bottom edges via clip-path and one drop shadow, all set in JetBrains Mono with dotted leaders, dashed rules and a double rule before the total. The barcode is decorative inline SVG. The COMPLIANT stamp is the one proprietary device: always green #0F7B4C, always the same three lines (POLICY CHECKS / COMPLIANT / 14/14 · month), rotated eight degrees, worn by an SVG dot mask, multiplied onto the paper so it reads as ink rather than a sticker; it is the only thing on the site not set straight. Photography is content, not palette: NPM's own people in natural colour with a neutral, slightly cool grade, eye level, rectangular crops on hairlines, captioned with name, role and 'Nonprofits I support'; no duotone, because the site has one colour and it is reserved for the stamp. Client work as documents: real receipts and reports reproduced at reading size with a date and a visible black mono REDACTED bar on anything withheld, never a blur. Beneficiary photography supplied by clients, dignity-first and consented, used sparingly with a credit line. Iconography is limited to arrows, the megaphone mark redrawn in ink only, and the mono glyph set (■ · →) used as separators in labels. There are no charts with axes anywhere: a utilisation figure is the three lines AD SPEND / GRANT CAP / UNSPENT, a click-through figure is a line item with 'GOOGLE'S FLOOR 5.00% · Cleared' under it. Client marks are typeset in mono uppercase; licensed logos are not needed.
motion: A thermal printer makes one motion, so the site makes one motion. On load the receipt feeds out of the printer: a ground-coloured cover steps down over the paper in 30 steps over 1.5s (CSS steps() timing, so it ticks like a print head) and the shadow appears with the paper; 220ms after the last line prints, the stamp lands, scaling from 1.3× to 1× with a slight overshoot (cubic-bezier .2,.9,.3,1.25). Both are CSS-only and already run in the mockups. The other paper objects (section 02's three receipts, section 04's fee receipt, the CTA band) feed the same way once on scroll-enter, with a tiny GSAP ScrollTrigger only for the trigger; the page is complete without JavaScript. Hover: the green button darkens to #0B5F3A, the ghost button's border turns green, links thicken their underline; no lift and no shadow change, paper does not float. Count-ups: none; numbers are printed, not animated. The eligibility checker slides horizontally between questions while its green progress rule fills; the honest not-eligible end card simply fades in. prefers-reduced-motion: the feed cover is removed, the stamp is static, transitions are disabled, all implemented in the mockups. No parallax, no WebGL, no Lottie, no marquee; the client roll is static.
mobile: The 390px page is a single column, a real phone layout rather than the desktop squeezed. Compact nav (56px, hairline beneath): mark and wordmark at 16px, a 40px green 'Book a call' button, a 44px menu target that hangs 10px into the gutter so its bars end flush. Then the mono eyebrow reduced to two items ('Free search ads for nonprofits · PAID BY GOOGLE'), h1 at 40px / 1.02 in three lines, a four-line deck at 16px, a full-width 48px green 'Book a free call · 15 MIN' button whose bottom sits at about 400px from the top, 'Am I eligible? · 4 QUESTIONS · NO EMAIL' at about 437px, and the fine-print line (flat fee, no % of spend, the $25 guarantee), all inside a 760px fold. Beneath the fold: the receipt at full width (358px of paper, about 470px tall, still perforated, still shadowed) condensed to six line items, the money block with PAID BY GOOGLE and DUE FROM YOU $0.00 at 24px, the tail beside a 150px stamp, and PLEASE RETAIN FOR YOUR BOARD; the barcode and the period rows are dropped on phones. The single trust element follows: 'On file for 780+ nonprofits · EACH MONTH' with the eight marks wrapping to three lines of mono. The Hurtado quote and the 'On file' line items move below the roll on phones. Key sections on phone: the terms table becomes stacked mono entries with the three headings as labels; section 02's three receipts stack; the two pricing receipts stack with Google's first; case studies stack with the KPI trio as a 3-up strip; the team grid is 2-up. Labels floor at 11px, the receipt's mono stays 12px, secondary gray holds AA on both grounds.
a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA is the target at every size, AAA for body. Measured on the actual grounds: ink #16181C on the counter #EFF1F3 15.7:1 and on paper 17.8:1; secondary #555B64 on the counter 6.05:1 and on paper 6.85:1 (11px labels pass AA with margin); green #0F7B4C on the counter 4.69:1 and on paper 5.31:1, used as text only at 11px and above with weight 600 or 700; white on green 5.31:1 and on the hover green 7.74:1. Smallest text is 11px (receipt notes, the receipt's tail, phone labels); the stamp's small lines render at 11.2px desktop and 11.1px phone, and the stamp is role=img with a label that states its three lines; body 17px desktop, 16px phone. Focus: a 3px #0F7B4C outline with 3px offset on every link and button (:focus-visible), visible on the counter, on paper and around the green button because of the offset gap. Targets: 48px primary buttons, 44px menu target, 40px compact nav button with clearance. Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion (feed cover removed, stamp static, transitions off). Text equivalents: the receipt is an aside labelled 'Sample monthly receipt' whose rows are real text in dl/dt/dd groups, so a screen reader hears 'Click-through rate 7.75%'; the dotted leaders are empty CSS pseudo-elements (no extra markup inside the dl, so it stays valid dt/dd groups), the barcode is aria-hidden decorative SVG, the megaphone mark and eyebrow squares are hidden. Colour is never the only carrier of meaning: 'Cleared' is a word beside the floor, not just a green tint; links are underlined; the active nav link is underlined as well as green; the stamp's meaning is in its text. mix-blend-mode multiply on the stamp is cosmetic; its text stays 5.31:1 green on white. The SAMPLE · ILLUSTRATIVE label is printed on the receipt itself, so the caveat travels with the object when it is forwarded.

heroCopy.eyebrow: Free search ads for nonprofits · $10,000 a month · Paid by Google
heroCopy.headline: $10,000 of Google Ads a month. Here's the receipt.
heroCopy.sub: Google gives eligible nonprofits $10,000 a month in search ads, and switches it off when click-through sits under 5% for two months running. Nonprofit Megaphone runs the account for 780+ nonprofits, keeps it compliant, and itemizes every dollar on a receipt you can forward to your board. Google pays for the ads. You pay a flat fee.

signatureMoments: The receipt feeding out of the printer on load, in 30 steps, then the COMPLIANT stamp landing with a small overshoot: the hero is a physical event, not a layout.
DUE FROM YOU $0.00 in 26px mono under a double rule, above PAID BY GOOGLE · MANAGED BY NONPROFIT MEGAPHONE: the business model as one line item.
'UNSPENT $13.60 · does not roll over. we'll get it.' The one joke on the page, printed in 11px faded ink, doing the job of a whole 'why us' section.
The COMPLIANT stamp: green ink multiplied onto the paper, worn by an SVG dot mask, rotated eight degrees, the only colour on the page and the only thing not set straight.

The foot of the copy column: Google's first Head of Ad Grants on one side of a hairline, 'ON FILE' line items with dotted leaders on the other, so the endorsement and the numbers are set in the receipt's own grammar.
dependencies: Consent from one client for a real, redacted monthly receipt to replace the SAMPLE in the hero, plus two more for section 02 (three verticals, one with a dip); until then the receipt keeps its SAMPLE · ILLUSTRATIVE label and is never attributed to a named client.

A monthly receipt in the reporting pipeline: a template the account team prints from real account data on the 1st of each month, with the policy-check count and the named lead, or the hero object is a prop.
Publish the flat fee (or a range) and the 0.00% of spend line for the fee receipt in section 04; confirm the 100% acquisition guarantee and the $25 meet-the-CEO wording as printed lines.

Leadership sign-off on the register: 'we'll get it', 'please retain for your board' and the stamp are jokes with a straight face; if the tone is softened to marketing copy the direction loses its edge.
Wordmark reset to Geist with the megaphone redrawn in ink only, a Webflow class set locked to no radii, no gradients and one shadow, and a check of Google Partner badge rules for the footer.
risks: Wit at the top of a nonprofit's buying journey: a receipt can read as flippant to a tired executive director if the copy around it is not plainly kind. The deck and the guarantee line carry the warmth; cutting them leaves a joke.

One green is a strict diet, and green already means 'success' in every dashboard; a Webflow editor adding a red error state or a yellow warning breaks the system at once. Locked classes are load-bearing.

Plausible numbers on a real-looking document invite scrutiny. The mockup labels the receipt SAMPLE · ILLUSTRATIVE on the paper itself; the build must print from real data or keep that label, and must never attribute sample figures to a named client.

A monospace receipt is text-dense on phones; the 390px contract (six line items, no barcode, 150px stamp) is in the mobile mockup and must be prototyped in Webflow rather than assumed. The clip-path perforation needs a rendering check in older Safari and in print.
references: Thermal till receipts themselves: centred header, dotted leaders, dashed rules, double rule before the total, barcode, the thank-you line; the grammar is borrowed whole.
Stripe's hosted receipts and Mercury's account statements for calm monospace finance documents on a neutral ground.
Vercel's Geist design system for the technical grotesk plus mono pairing on cool gray and its no-gradient discipline.
The 'receipts' idiom (Costco and CVS receipt culture, 'show me the receipts') for the idea that a receipt is the most trusted document ordinary people handle.
Annie Atkins's prop design for Wes Anderson (stamps, dockets, permits) for the register of the COMPLIANT stamp.
